content.text: What Each Option Actually Offers: Plugins online

Let's look at the features each of these platforms provides for digital sellers. Stripe is a popular payment gateway that handles transactions and provides analytics, but it's not available in many countries. PayPal, on the other hand, offers a more comprehensive suite of tools, including invoicing and shipping integrations, but its account suspension policies have left many sellers vulnerable. Gumroad and Lemon Squeezy are e-commerce platforms that allow creators to sell digital products, but they also come with their own set of restrictions and fees. In contrast, a sovereign commerce infrastructure like COREMERCH provides a base-layer solution that gives creators full control over their commerce stack, including hosting, backend logic, order storage, and file delivery.
How They Handle Restricted Countries

When it comes to restricted countries, Stripe has a limited presence, operating in only 46 out of 195 countries. PayPal, on the other hand, has been known to suspend accounts and hold funds for up to 180 days without appeal, leaving sellers in a precarious position. Gumroad and Lemon Squeezy also have their own set of restrictions and limitations when it comes to serving creators in restricted countries. In contrast, a sovereign commerce infrastructure like COREMERCH is designed to operate in even the most restricted countries, providing a permanent solution to this problem.
Payment Speed, Fees, and Real Costs

When it comes to payment speed, fees, and real costs, each platform has its own set of trade-offs. Stripe and PayPal charge transaction fees ranging from 2.9% + 30¢ to 3.4% + 30¢ per transaction, while Gumroad and Lemon Squeezy charge fees ranging from 3.5% + 30¢ to 8% + 30¢ per transaction. In contrast, a sovereign commerce infrastructure like COREMERCH charges a flat fee of 0.5% per transaction, making it a more cost-effective option for digital sellers.
